raw_record.question_text:
In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: First describe the image components. For the left organic fragment, count only non-H bonds: two N–C substituent bonds, one N–C carbonyl bond, and one C=O bond, giving 4. Exclude the C–H bond on the carbonyl carbon. For the phosphorus fragment, count P=O plus three P–Cl bonds, giving 4. Disregard the curved arrows. Add the two component counts: 4 + 4 = 8.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: In skeletal chemical drawings, line ends can represent carbons; a displayed single, double, or triple bond between non-hydrogen atoms is counted as one bond occurrence for this question. Bonds to hydrogen are excluded, and arrows are not bonds.
